overview: This file documents Allied regulation of Japanese fishing and whaling after World War II. It traces changes to authorized fishing grounds, Korean and Soviet objections, territorial claims in the Kurils, Japanese inspection and conservation measures, Chinese seizures of fishing vessels, proposed U.S. naval patrols, and Antarctic whaling oversight. Correspondence, directives, reports, maps, and firsthand accounts show how fisheries policy became a diplomatic and security issue.
interest: Firsthand seizure accounts and proposed fishing boundaries reveal how maritime resources shaped postwar diplomacy and territorial disputes.
